comments.author: bravura
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Good books on machine learning?
comments.why_zh: 由一位备受尊敬的机器学习研究者提供的视频讲座，可作为读书之外的替代选择
comments.quote_zh: 你也可以看看 Andrew Ng 的视频讲座
comments.text_zh: 我附议推荐 Bishop。它是这个领域的标准教材。它才出版两年，而且 Bishop 会教你按如今这个领域的实际做法来理解机器学习。在我这个十四人的实验室里，我们大概有六本 Bishop。我不明白 Bishop 哪里不实用。如果你只是想闭着眼睛找一个现成的机器学习实现来用，那是另一回事。机器学习被描述为对偏置（bias）的研究。如果你想弄明白什么时候该选某种技术、并培养出合适的偏置，那就读 Bishop。Hastie、Tibshirani 和 Friedman 的《The Elements of Statistical Learning》更多是从统计学家的视角出发。它的处理方式只是没那么全面，而且也更过时一些。你也可以看看 Andrew Ng 的视频讲座：[VIDEO] 他在这个领域非常受尊敬。对某些学生来说，看讲座可能比读书更合适。
comments.text: I second the nomination of Bishop. It is the standard text. It is only two years old, and Bishop will teach you machine learning the way that the field practices it nowadays. In my lab of fourteen people, we must have six or so copies of Bishop. I don't understand what is impractical about Bishop. If you are looking blindly to use an off-the-shelf machine learning implementation, that's one thing. Machine Learning has been described as the study of bias. If you want to understand when to pick certain techniques, and develop appropriate biases, then read Bishop. "The Elements of Statistical Learning" by Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman gives more of a statistician's approach. The treatment is simply less broad, and also more dated. You can also look at Andrew Ng's video lectures: [VIDEO] He is very well-respected in the field. For certain students, watching a lecture may be preferable to reading a book.

comments.author: joaogui1
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Full-on machine learning for 2020, what are the best resources?
comments.quote_zh: Andrew Ng 的机器学习课程，大多数人推荐的入门选择
comments.text_zh: 机器学习：* [VIDEO]：Andrew Ng 的机器学习课程，大多数人推荐的入门选择 * [LINK]：更偏向 kaggle，但也更现代，并且有有趣的项目。同时学这两门课，做好笔记，写有用的抽认卡，最重要的是把所有练习和项目都做完。深度学习 * [LINK]——非常实操，先从“Practical Deep Learning for Coders”开始，然后再学“Advanced Deep Learning for coders” * [LINK]：更偏自下而上的方式，有助于更好地理解理论。并行学习这两门课（一开始你可以先试 2 周 coursera，然后试一门 fastai，之后就只是在两者之间交替），做笔记，写好的抽认卡，最重要的是做练习和项目。这之后你就完成了入门，下一步取决于你对哪个领域最感兴趣；现在拿到太多资源会极其令人困惑，所以我建议你在学完上述资源后再发一个后续帖子。另外，作为非 ML 的内容，我推荐 Scott Young 的 Ultralearning 和 Azeria 的自我提升文章（[LINK]）。
comments.text: Machine Learning: * [VIDEO] : Andrew Ng's machine Learning course, the recommended entry point by most people * [LINK] : More kaggle focused, but also more modern and has interesting projects Do both courses simultaneously, take good notes, write useful flashcards, and above all do all the exercises and projects Deep Learning * [LINK] - Very hands-on, begin with " Practical Deep Learning for Coders" and then "Advanced Deep Learning for coders" * [LINK] : More bottom-up approach, helps to understand the theory better Do those two courses in parallel (you can try 2 weeks of coursera followed by one of fastai in the beginning, and then just alternate between them), take notes, write good flashcards and above all do the exercises and projects. After that you will be done with the beginning, your next step will depend on what area interested you the most, and getting way too many resources right now can be extremely confusing, so I would recommend doing a follow-up post after you worked through the above resources. Also as non-ML stuff I recommend Scott Young's Ultralearning and Azeria's self improvement posts ( [LINK] )
